correctness.rationale: For every n,k positive, structural induction using classical evaluation at maximal worlds proves rooted formula truth depends only on the root color a and the set S of distinct maximal-world colors. Atoms distinguish unequal a; the intuitionistic negated classical minterm for t is true at root iff t is absent from S, so unequal S are distinguished. All admissible pairs are realizable, giving the exact binomial count and stabilization. Duplicating leaf colors preserves every formula. The explicit formula Theta(n,k), a disjunction of negated disjunctions of minterms outside k-sets, is valid everywhere on F_k and refuted at root of F_{k+1} with k+1 distinct colors whenever k<2^n. This yields the sharp logarithmic variable threshold. A standalone program exhaustively checked 43,291 sample valuations/types, 1,013 separating evaluations, and 999 full formula-validity cases, but finite tests are not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The problem asks a natural model-theoretic question—exactly how many finite-variable rooted theories distinct branch types generate on canonical two-level intermediate-logic frames, and when additional branching becomes invisible? The result gives all cases, a closed binomial census, the complete sharp hierarchy of n-variable logics, and explicit uniform separating formulas. This motivates finite-model compression and local tabularity; it is not an arbitrary finite slice, a mere negative check, or an assertion about unproved generalized frames.
